answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, an agent network inspecting a harbor jetty, tracking saffron trade, or mapping a spiral duct can enforce proof of capacity. Each agent must commit cryptographic plots to persistent storage and answer periodic latency-bounded audit queries. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of dedicating real disk volume and read bandwidth per counterfeit identity. However, this burden excludes storage-limited edge agents and incentivizes centralized hardware pooling.
